import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "gamma": 0.97}

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.half = int(spec.Y) // 2
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(2 * spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        h = self.half
        rolled = torch.cat([obs[:, :, h:], obs[:, :, :h]], dim=2)
        s = self.stem(torch.cat([obs, rolled], dim=1))
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.hypothesis: After a linear 1x1 stem, four channel groups each get their own learned Linear over all Y*X cells. The original features are kept alongside. This lets the net learn any cell-to-cell remapping (such as the observed Y/2 roll) without hand-coding it, so it should carry over to other grid sizes. import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "gamma": 0.97}

STEM = 64
GROUPS = 4
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class TokenMix(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, n, groups):
        super().__init__()
        self.groups = groups
        self.cg = c // groups
        self.lins = nn.ModuleList([nn.Linear(n, n) for _ in range(groups)])

    def forward(self, h):
        b, c, y, x = h.shape
        t = h.reshape(b, c, y * x)
        outs = []
        for i, lin in enumerate(self.lins):
            outs.append(lin(t[:, i * self.cg:(i + 1) * self.cg]))
        return torch.cat(outs, dim=1).reshape(b, self.groups * self.cg, y, x)


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        n = int(spec.Y) * int(spec.X)
        self.inp = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1)
        self.tmix = TokenMix(STEM, n, GROUPS)
        self.post = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(2 * STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        a = self.inp(obs)
        m = self.tmix(a)
        s = self.post(F.relu(torch.cat([a, m], dim=1)))
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

        self.cg = c // groups
        self.ly = nn.ModuleList([nn.Linear(ny, ny) for _ in range(groups)])
        self.lx = nn.ModuleList([nn.Linear(nx, nx) for _ in range(groups)])

            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))

        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

        a = self.inp(obs)
        m = self.mix1(a)

        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))

        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)

trials.hypothesis: The placement head sees only local 5x5 context. Choosing the right order (supports before overhangs, which region next) depends on the whole board. A pooled global vector, passed through a learned linear layer, is added to every cell's features before the placement head. The extra compute is negligible, so the step count stays the same. Dev success above 0.89 would support this. No gain or a drop would refute the claim that a lack of global context limits placement.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "gamma": 0.97}

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.half = int(spec.Y) // 2
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(2 * spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.pre = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.bcast = nn.Linear(64, WIDTH)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        h = self.half
        rolled = torch.cat([obs[:, :, h:], obs[:, :, :h]], dim=2)
        s = self.stem(torch.cat([obs, rolled], dim=1))
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        g0 = self.pre(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        f2 = F.relu(f + self.bcast(g0)[:, :, None, None])
        place = self.head(f2)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f2.mean((2, 3)), f2.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

COL = 48

HID = 32

import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 24
HID = 24


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()

        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p

                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "gamma": 0.97, "ppo_epochs": 3}

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)

            nn.Conv2d(2 * spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())

        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)

        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

        h = self.half
        rolled = torch.cat([obs[:, :, h:], obs[:, :, :h]], dim=2)
        s = self.stem(torch.cat([obs, rolled], dim=1))

analyses.1: No trials have run yet. The starting network learned to end every episode with DONE at once: episode length fell to 1.0 by mid-training and dev success was 0. The traces explain why. The target height map in the observation is the true design rolled cyclically by Y/2 rows (observed row r = design row r+4, columns unchanged). Rewards and placements use the true frame. The starting network only sees a 5x5 neighbourhood, so it cannot match a target cell with the build cell 4 rows away. Placing without that information loses reward, and DONE (reward 0) wins. The build, missing and extra channels may also be rolled; I can't tell yet. So this round tests whether moving information across the grid fixes it. One candidate adds a fixed roll as a diagnostic. Two add learned global mixing, which handles any frame mix-up and should carry over to other grid sizes. All three use the same recipe: n_envs 128, so twice as many updates, and gamma 0.97.
analyses.2: The starting network and the two learned-mixing networks all collapsed to choosing DONE at once, or nearly so. The fixed half-roll network reached 0.89 (seeds 0.94 and 0.85). The diagnostic traces show why: the observed target is the true design shifted cyclically by Y/2 rows. Giving the network a copy of the input rolled back into line is what made learning possible; the learned full and axial mixing did not find the shift within the budget. The successful run is near-perfect but not complete: mean IoU 0.991 and 0.2 cells placed outside the target per episode. Its training success was still rising at the end (0.81 at 75%, 0.94 at 100%), so it looks short of samples. This round, each candidate makes one change to the r1c1 file: fewer PPO epochs to get more samples, a longer credit horizon so the +1 exact-build bonus counts for more, and a cheap global-context broadcast into the per-cell features.
analyses.3: The observed target is shifted by Y/2 rows. Rolling the input by Y//2 (r1c1) took the agent from always pressing DONE to 0.89 dev success (0.94 and 0.85 per seed). Learned remapping, full (r1c2) or axial (r1c3), did not find the shift within budget. On top of the roll, gamma 0.99 (0.85) and global broadcast (0.87) are within seed noise of 0.89, so neither helped. Two PPO epochs (0.66) gave one bad seed: more samples did not make up for less reuse per sample. With the roll, IoU is about 0.99 and training success was still rising at the end, so the limit is how well the agent learns per sample, not perception. Next tests: more gradient steps on the same samples (smaller minibatches), a higher learning rate, and a deeper trunk with a dilated convolution for larger receptive field, at the cost of fewer steps.
analyses.4: The observed target is shifted Y/2 rows away from the action frame. Without the half-roll input, training collapses to DONE. Learned mixing over cells (r1c2, r1c3) did not find the shift within the budget. With the roll, every variant scores between 0.85 and 0.89. These changes were r2c2 (gamma 0.99), r2c3 (global broadcast), r3c1 (32 minibatches) and r3c2 (lr 2e-3). r2c1 (2 epochs, 0.656) hurt, and r3c3 (a deeper net that cost samples, 0.738) hurt too. r1c1's 0.89 rests on one seed at 0.94 and one at 0.85, so its true mean is probably about 0.87. All variants show training success still rising at the end and IoU near 0.99, so the remaining failures are small errors in order or placement. The last round tests three cheap recipe changes that may speed late convergence without costing samples: lower entropy, 3 PPO epochs, and smaller, fresher updates.
